correctness.rationale: The Schur-orthogonality diagonalization on SO(3) uses probability measures and one positive Fourier mode; Legendre differentiation gives exact even and odd formulas. Wallis recurrence and limit prove all strict eigenvalue bounds and sharp asymptotic. Smooth small spherical-harmonic support perturbations prove the convex sharpness and absence of stronger-Sobolev estimates. Independent exact rational zonal integrals through degree 22 check normalization and formulas but are not substitutes for the infinite analytic proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 problem establishes only exact rigidity of spherical projection support data. A sharp rate for approximate two-frequency rotational symmetry, its optimal 2/pi constant, full singular-value profile and the necessity of a half-order derivative loss constitute a meaningful quantitative inverse-geometric stability result. Sharpness holds on smooth strictly convex near-spherical bodies; the spectral obstruction matters for imperfect observations.
